name: Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir
drug_class: HCV NS3/4A protease inhibitor plus NS5A inhibitor (fixed-dose combination)
route_note: three tablets once daily with food (or pellets for children) for 8 weeks in most patients

discovery.note: Second-generation pangenotypic protease and NS5A inhibitors with activity against common resistance variants.

tagline: Eight-week, pangenotypic hepatitis C cure that is safe in kidney disease
summary: Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir is a fixed-dose combination of an NS3/4A protease inhibitor and an NS5A inhibitor that cures hepatitis C of all genotypes, usually in 8 weeks. It is not cleared by the kidneys, so it can be used in severe kidney disease and dialysis. Like other protease-inhibitor regimens, it is not used in decompensated cirrhosis.
mechanism: Glecaprevir inhibits the NS3/4A serine protease, which cleaves the HCV polyprotein into the non-structural proteins needed for replication.

Pibrentasvir binds NS5A, a phosphoprotein essential for forming the viral replication complex and assembling virions. Combining two targets with high potency against resistant variants gives cure rates around 95–99% in clinical trials.
uses: Chronic hepatitis C, all genotypes, in adults and children aged 3 years and older without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis
Retreatment of patients previously treated with an NS5A or NS3/4A inhibitor (but not both)

history.title: EU approval
history.detail: The European Commission approves Maviret in July 2017.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Mavyret in August 2017 as the first 8-week pangenotypic regimen for treatment-naive patients without cirrhosis.

history.title: Compensated cirrhosis
history.detail: The 8-week course is extended to treatment-naive patients with compensated cirrhosis; paediatric approval follows.

history.title: Young children
history.detail: Oral pellets are approved in the US for children aged 3 years and older.

history.title: Acute hepatitis C
history.detail: The FDA approves Mavyret for acute HCV infection, the first DAA labelled for that use.

pk.half_life: glecaprevir about 6 h; pibrentasvir about 13 h
pk.metabolism: glecaprevir partly by CYP3A; pibrentasvir minimal; both biliary

serious: hepatitis B reactivation in co-infected patients
hepatic decompensation in patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment or prior decompensation
safety.boxed_warning: Risk of hepatitis B virus reactivation, sometimes fulminant, in patients co-infected with HCV and HBV; test for HBV before starting (US label).

facts: Because it is not renally cleared, no dose adjustment is needed in any stage of chronic kidney disease, including dialysis.
It is contraindicated with atazanavir and rifampicin.
